children: By Anita Hamilton and Callum Keown

Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has made an $11.6 billion deal with cloud infrastructure firm Akamai for its computing services for the next seven years, Akamai announced, with an option to expand the deal by another $9 billion if more compute is needed.

Akamai stock rose more than 21% to $133.84 in premarket trading on Friday. Anthropic, currently not publicly traded, filed confidential paperwork in June for an IPO, and the official filing is expected soon.

AI companies are in an all-out race for more compute, which is the hardware needed to train and run their models. The deal will "support Anthropic's accelerating CPU workload demands by leveraging Akamai Cloud's distributed AI infrastructure and software," Akamai said.
The cloud company said that the deal will involve $5.5 billion in new capital expenditures, including buying memory, with $1.6 billion of that in 2026.

As part of the deal, Akamai has issued a warrant to Anthropic giving it the right to exercise 7.7 million shares of Akamai common stock-5% of those outstanding-at the price of $111.33 each. Some of the stock vests today, with the rest contingent on expanding the deal by the additional $9 billion.
Anthropic didn't immediately reply to Barron's request for comment.
